finding.title: Extract the duplicated _extractFirebaseCode regex parser out of MagicLinkService and UpgradeToCloudService
finding.rule: Fowler: duplicated code; layering tension with Rule 3
finding.why: Both files independently reimplement 'parse a Firebase error code out of an exception's toString()' via the identical regex, because Rule 3 blocks these features/account/{domain,data} files from importing FirebaseAuthException directly and matching its typed .code field. The fallback is fragile: if a Firebase Auth SDK bump changes the exception's string format so it no longer wraps the code in literal brackets, _extractFirebaseCode silently returns null everywhere at once — in upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart this means the 'email-already-in-use' retry-merge branch falls through to rethrow, and the guided merge flow silently stops firing, surfacing a raw exception to the user instead. The same helper is also duplicated at 3 more sites repo-wide (signup_screen.dart, sign_in_controller.dart, upgrade_to_cloud_screen.dart), confirming this is a systemic gap rather than a one-off.
finding.recommendation: Factor the regex parser into one shared, unit-tested helper (e.g. core/utils/firebase_error_code.dart, which only touches strings so it doesn't trip Rule 3) that all current call sites import.
acceptance_criteria: one shared, unit-tested extractFirebaseCode(Object e) utility exists
magic_link_service.dart and upgrade_to_cloud_service.dart delegate to it instead of each defining their own regex copy

finding.title: Remove the fixed height:32 on OfflineTopBanner's Container so large text-scale doesn't clip it
finding.rule: AX-4 (no fixed heights on text wrappers)
finding.why: The banner's Container is given a tight height:32 which forces the same tight cross-axis height onto the Row wrapping the cloud-off Icon and the offline-message Text. The app sets no textScaler clamp anywhere (grep-confirmed repo-wide), so under a standard OS large-text accessibility setting the Text needs more than 32 logical pixels; because Container does not clip by default, the text would paint outside the 32px band, visually overlapping the AppBar/content around it rather than wrapping or growing the banner.
finding.recommendation: Let the banner size to its child's intrinsic height (drop the fixed height, or express it as a minHeight), and add a widget test that pumps OfflineTopBanner under a scaled MediaQuery (TextScaler.linear(1.6)+) and asserts no overflow/clip.
acceptance_criteria: a widget/golden test pumps OfflineTopBanner at textScaler >= 1.6x and asserts the rendered content fits within its layout bounds
the banner Container no longer hard-codes height:32

finding.title: Move account_picker_switch_test.dart into test/.../presentation/screens/ to match its siblings
finding.why: account_picker_switch_test.dart sits directly under test/features/account/presentation/, while its three siblings covering the exact same AccountPickerScreen (account_picker_an4_test.dart, account_picker_local_data_missing_test.dart, account_picker_screen_l1_test.dart) correctly live one level deeper under presentation/screens/, matching lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_picker_screen.dart. It's the only one of the four out of place, making it easy to miss when scanning the screens/ directory for everything that covers this screen.
acceptance_criteria: account_picker_switch_test.dart is located under test/features/account/presentation/screens/, matching its three sibling files

finding.title: Replace magic_link_service_test.dart's 20 fixed-delay waits with a deterministic completion signal
finding.why: This file uses plain test() (no fakeAsync/tester.runAsync wrapper), so all 20 of these are real wall-clock waits used to let the fake uriLinkStream's listener finish processing before the following assertions run. Each adds ~50ms of guaranteed dead time (~1s total for this file), and because 50ms is a guess rather than a guarantee, the assertions are one slow/contended CI runner away from a flaky false failure if the listener callback hasn't finished when the wait ends.
finding.recommendation: Await an explicit completion signal instead — e.g. have the test await a Completer that the fake onSignedIn/mock callback completes, rather than guessing a fixed sleep.
acceptance_criteria: magic_link_service_test.dart's stream-driven tests await an explicit completion signal (e.g. a Completer) instead of a fixed-millisecond Future.delayed

finding.title: Give SignInActions' TapGestureRecognizer a disposal owner instead of rebuilding it every build()
finding.why: SignInActions is a StatelessWidget, so every build() (e.g. each time isLoading flips) allocates a brand-new TapGestureRecognizer that nothing ever calls .dispose() on. The framework does not manage recognizer lifecycle automatically; Flutter's own guidance is to create such recognizers once in a State and dispose them in State.dispose(). The same pattern also exists in signup_screen.dart:825, so it's a small but repeated hygiene gap, not a one-off typo.
finding.recommendation: Hoist the 'Register' tap handling into a small stateful owner (or the already-stateful parent SignInScreen) that creates the TapGestureRecognizer once and disposes it in dispose().
acceptance_criteria: the TapGestureRecognizer used for the Register span is created once and disposed via a State.dispose() rather than reallocated on every SignInActions.build()
